events.title: The Abbasids crush an Alid revolt at the Battle of Fakhkh
events.description: Abbasid forces crushed an Alid revolt led by al-Husayn ibn Ali, a descendant of Hasan ibn Ali, near Mecca; al-Husayn and many of his followers were killed. A survivor, Idris ibn Abd Allah, fled to Morocco and founded the Idrisid dynasty.

events.title: An Abbasid army sets out from Raqqa to invade Asia Minor
events.description: The army of Caliph Harun al-Rashid, far larger than any assembled before, left Raqqa, crossed Cilicia and the Taurus Mountains and invaded Byzantine Cappadocia. The Byzantine losses, including the sack of Herakleia, forced Emperor Nikephoros to seek peace.

events.title: Bari's Greek citizens deliver the city to the Byzantine catepan
events.description: The Greek citizens of Bari rose against the Lombard rebels led by Melus and delivered the city to Basil Mesardonites, the Byzantine catepan of Italy, who entered it and re-established Byzantine authority.

events.title: Henry VIII marries Catherine of Aragon
events.description: Weeks after his accession, Henry married his brother Arthur's widow at Greenwich. Their failure to produce a surviving son later led Henry to break with Rome.

events.title: Congress appoints a committee to draft a declaration of independence
events.description: Thomas Jefferson, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Roger Sherman and Robert Livingston formed the Committee of Five. Jefferson wrote the first draft.
events.html: Thomas Jefferson, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Roger Sherman and Robert Livingston formed the Committee of Five. Jefferson wrote the first draft.

events.title: Thích Quảng Đức burns himself to death in Saigon
events.description: The Buddhist monk set himself alight at a busy junction to protest the Diem government's treatment of Buddhists. Malcolm Browne's photograph shocked the world.
events.html: The Buddhist monk set himself alight at a busy junction to protest the Diem government's treatment of Buddhists. Malcolm Browne's photograph shocked the world.

events.title: George Wallace stands in the schoolhouse door
events.description: Alabama's governor blocked the entrance to the University of Alabama to stop two Black students enrolling, then stood aside when federalised Guard troops arrived. Kennedy addressed the nation on civil rights that night.

events.title: Timothy McVeigh is executed for the Oklahoma City bombing
events.description: McVeigh was put to death by lethal injection in Terre Haute, Indiana. It was the first federal execution in the United States since 1963.
